rules.statement: The COL1A1 arginine-to-cysteine change Arg134Cys has been reported in an EDS/OI overlap phenotype.

sources.credit: GeneReviews® © 1993-2026 University of Washington, Seattle (https://www.genereviews.org); excerpt reproduced verbatim for noncommercial research
sources.quote: EDS/OI overlap phenotypes (OMIM 619115) Three arginine-to-cysteine changes (Arg134Cys, Arg915Cys, & Arg396Cys) in COL1A1 have been reported in an EDS phenotype w/a propensity to arterial rupture in early adulthood [Malfait et al 2007].

review.reason: "have been reported" does not support "points to": the source says three arginine-to-cysteine changes have been reported in an EDS phenotype, which is a report, not a general association. The rule layer promotes an OMIM disease to a branch, and that step needs more than one reported observation. The support check said the same three times (conclusion partially supported 3:0).

rules.narrowed: narrowed 2026-11-05 (review): the source names the arginine-to-cysteine change Arg134Cys, so the rule no longer fires on any other substitution at residue 134.

items.item: Condition: the rule is about COL1A1 variants that are missense variants and that replace Arg at protein residue 134 with Cys.
items.reason: The quote names COL1A1 and an arginine-to-cysteine change at Arg134Cys, matching the stated substitution.

items.item: Conclusion: such variants point to combined osteogenesis imperfecta and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome 1 (also called: OIEDS Syndrome 1; OIEDS1).
items.reason: The quote supports an EDS/OI overlap phenotype but does not name combined OI and EDS syndrome 1 or OIEDS1.

items.item: Scope: this is stated as a general association for such COL1A1 variants, not only for a single reported patient or family, and not only as a difference in frequency between patient groups.
items.reason: The quote says three such changes have been reported, but it does not explicitly state a general association or clarify patient/family scope.

rules.statement: Loss of exon 6 of COL1A1 results in arthrochalasia EDS.

sources.credit: GeneReviews® © 1993-2026 University of Washington, Seattle (https://www.genereviews.org); excerpt reproduced verbatim for noncommercial research
sources.quote: Arthrochalasia EDS results from loss of exon 6 of either COL1A1 or COL1A2.

review.reason: The source states that arthrochalasia EDS results from LOSS of exon 6, but deciding which variants cause that loss needs splice prediction, which step 1 does not do (decision 2026-11-05: splice prediction is not connected). The narrowed condition therefore stands in for the source rather than following it, and the support check marked the condition item down for exactly that (2:1). Also, the quote names arthrochalasia EDS without the type or the synonyms of OMIM 130060.

rules.narrowed: narrowed 2026-11-05 (review): the source is about LOSS of exon 6, so the rule now fires only on a deletion covering exon 6 or a splice variant at its boundary, never on a coding change inside the exon.

items.item: Condition: the rule is about COL1A1 variants that remove the whole of exon 6 (a deletion covering it, or a splice variant at its boundary).
items.reason: The quote states loss of exon 6 but not the specific deletion-covering or splice-boundary variant details.

items.item: Conclusion: such variants point to Ehlers-Danlos syndrome arthrochalasia type 1 (also called: EDS VIIA; EDSARTH1; Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type 7A).
items.reason: The quote supports Arthrochalasia EDS generally, but does not specify type 1 or the listed synonyms.

items.item: Scope: this is stated as a general association for such COL1A1 variants, not only for a single reported patient or family, and not only as a difference in frequency between patient groups.
items.reason: The quote states a general causal association for COL1A1 exon 6 loss, not a single case or frequency difference.
